title: Building Test Collections: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Building Test Collections: Visual Guide

1. Sample The Traffic | The bridge from P@k, MAP, MRR and nDCG to the query set they average over: toggle uniform versus stratified sampling and drag the set size, watching per-class counts, macro versus traffic-weighted nDCG, and which strata are diagnosable at all. | A uniform sample of logs spends 60 percent of its budget on navigational queries and leaves too few compliance queries to see a 30-point regression; stratified sampling reserves capacity and records the weights that recover the traffic estimate.

2. Depth Of The Pool | Pooling made concrete: switch pool contributors (BM25, a second lexical variant, freshness, specialised fields, dense semantic, random controls) and set the depth, then watch the pool size, which of a challenger's six relevant documents get judged, and the measured nDCG@10 of incumbent versus challenger. | Unjudged means scored as irrelevant, so a lexical-only pool makes a dense challenger lose a comparison it should win — and if the winner changes as depth grows, the shallow pool was weak evidence.

3. Fooling The Judge | An LLM relevance judge under paired-counterexample testing: toggle surface features of one document (shown first, long and repetitive, polished, citation-formatted, adversarial) plus two mitigations (blind and randomise, require verified evidence) and read the grade the judge gives against the human grade, with each feature's measured inflation. | Position, verbosity, style and authority-by-formatting each move the grade without moving relevance; blinding kills position bias and verified evidence catches hallucinated support, which no amount of reading a confident rationale will.

4. Grade Drift Dial | Calibration error turned into metric error: dial how many grade-2 documents the judge calls 3 and how many grade-1s it calls 0, switch the gain function between 2^g-1, linear and a binary collapse, and compare the true nDCG with the judge's. | Exponential gain makes grade 3 worth 7 against grade 2's 3, so one grade of drift near the top reweights a document by 2.33x — which is why calibration is reported as a confusion matrix and why collapsing grades is a real fix.

5. Benchmark Transfer | MS MARCO and BEIR read against a chosen product profile (support search with error codes, multilingual catalogue, biomedical claims, English web Q&A), with a contamination-and-test-set-tuning toggle that downgrades every public row; tap a row for the mechanism. | Public benchmarks verify implementations and compare broad approaches, but transfer only where language, lexical exactness, terminology, freshness and intent match — the private golden set is what decides product questions.
